minutes.headline: Select Board put a school override placeholder on the warrant and ballot and voted a single tax rate.
minutes.summary: Long public comment on the school override, mostly urging support. A joint session with the Board of Assessors ended in a single tax rate vote and acceptance of a warrant article lowering the low-income senior exemption age. The board suspended its 60-day ballot policy so override language can be finalized later in March, and a member asked to discuss ARPA funds for school items.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted by roll call to adopt a single tax rate and took no action on open space, residential exemption or small commercial exemption.
The board accepted the warrant article lowering the low-income senior exemption age and sent it to Town Counsel to modify the language.
The board suspended its 60-day notice policy for ballot questions, so override language can be finalized later.
The school override placeholder stays on the warrant, with a special meeting targeted for March 26 to settle the language and the number.
The school committee's override request was described as a little over a million dollars, with the number still moving.

why_it_matters: The single tax rate means residential and commercial property are taxed at the same rate, which sets how the levy is split among tax bills.
The school override is a question residents will be asked to vote on, and its wording and size are not yet fixed.
Lowering the senior exemption age would widen who qualifies for a tax break, with the cost absorbed within the town's overlay account.
watch_next: Special meeting targeted for March 26 to finalize the override language and number.
Town Counsel's revised language for the senior exemption warrant article.
